overview: This House resolution changes how "pairs" are announced during the current Congress. A pair is an informal agreement between two members on opposite sides of a vote, often when one of them will be absent, so that their positions are put on the record even though they don't vote. Under this resolution, the House Clerk announces pairs from a written list signed by the member making the arrangement, just before the result of a vote is announced, and the list is printed in the Congressional Record. Pairs are announced only once per legislative day. It was adopted on April 8, 2025, as part of House Resolution 294.
for: Supporters say it gives members who cannot be present a simple, documented way to show how they would have voted, keeping the public record more complete.
against: Critics say pairing is no substitute for actually voting, since a pair doesn't count toward the outcome, and that the change offers limited help to members who cannot be in Washington.
